Problem 665. Indirect effects in a food chain: case 5
Knowledge context.
Ecosystems contain dependency networks. A change at one point can propagate indirectly through several links.
Given facts.

Food relation: rabbit eats grass; fox eats rabbit; eagle eats fox. Classroom rule: if a food source sharply decreases and no alternative food is given, the consumer may also decrease. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.
Follow dependency arrows from food to consumer. The rule supports possible directional effects, not exact population numbers. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
If rabbit sharply decreases, which later populations may be indirectly affected according to the rule? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. fox depends directly on rabbit, so it may decrease. 2. eagle depends on fox, so it may also be indirectly affected. 3. grass is food for rabbit; the stated rule does not imply it decreases for the same reason. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Answer.
fox may decrease directly and eagle may be affected indirectly. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
Indirect effects require following the direction of dependency and respecting the limits of the stated model.
Formal model.
Directed dependency graph; propagate a qualitative decrease along outgoing dependency links.
N9. Renewable resources and sustainable use
Problem 666. Regeneration and harvest: case 1
Knowledge context.
Renewable does not mean unlimited. A resource can decline when use exceeds regeneration.
Given facts.
A forest resource starts at 130 units. Each year it regenerates 12 units and people harvest 11 units. Assume these amounts stay constant for 3 years and no other changes occur.
Rules.
Annual net change = regeneration − harvest. In this simplified model, use is sustainable over the period if stock does not decline.
Task.
What is the stock after 3 years, and is the harvest sustainable under this classroom definition?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Annual net change=12−11=1. 2. Three-year change=3. 3. Final stock=130+(3)=133. 4. Compare final stock with starting stock.
Answer.
133 units; sustainable under the stated definition.
Knowledge takeaway.
Sustainability is a balance between renewal and extraction over time.
Formal model.
Stock-flow model with regeneration and harvest; test non-decreasing stock.

Problem 668. Regeneration and harvest: case 3
Knowledge context.
Renewable does not mean unlimited. A resource can decline when use exceeds regeneration.
Given facts.
A forest resource starts at 130 units. Each year it regenerates 16 units and people harvest 17 units. Assume these amounts stay constant for 3 years and no other changes occur.
Rules.
Annual net change = regeneration − harvest. In this simplified model, use is sustainable over the period if stock does not decline.
Task.
What is the stock after 3 years, and is the harvest sustainable under this classroom definition?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Annual net change=16−17=-1. 2. Three-year change=-3. 3. Final stock=130+(-3)=127. 4. Compare final stock with starting stock.

127 units; not sustainable under the stated definition.
